messages.author: 8393b4780d0d6e0b
messages.subject: Problem with pdf plots
parts:
Hi Nick,

I'm running R version 3.5.1 in RStudio, and BioGeoBEARS 1.1. I've double checked and have no other versions of R or BioGeoBEARS installed on my computer (at least as far as I can tell). I've run a few BioGeoBEARs analyses recently and am having a problem with pdf plots. Everything runs fine, but the pdf plots don't seem to stop saving. By which I mean, when I run the plot code for DEC & DEC+J, the pdf doesn't automatically open (Adobe Reader tells me the document is currently in use by another programme). Then I go ahead and run DIVALIKE and DIVALIKE+J, and plot. The plot again doesn't work. Same for BAYAREALIKE. But pdfs are being saved. When I go to open the pdfs after the analysis, they've either printed into the wrong file - so the  DIVALIKE analyses are in the BAYAREALIKE file - or the file is blank, or contains the last thing I did in R (my DEC results contain a supertree for another analysis, currently. This also happened to my student recently using a different machine but the same code. Saving used to work fine with the exact same code (I'm using your example code) so I have literally no clue what is going on (and I'm not very good at R!). Are you able to help at all?

Code and an example of the results attached.

Many thanks.

Susie

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Problem with pdf plots
parts:
Hi - I'm out of the office today, but probably the issue is just with closing the writing of the pdf -- the dev.off() command.

Here's an example:

==================
# Look at your phylogeny (plots to a PDF, which avoids issues with multiple graphics in same window):
pdffn = "tree.pdf"
pdf(file=pdffn, width=9, height=12)

tr = read.tree(trfn)
tr
plot(tr)
title("Example Psychotria phylogeny from Ree & Smith (2008)")
axisPhylo() # plots timescale

dev.off()
cmdstr = paste0("open ", pdffn)
system(cmdstr)
==================

...if you accidentally skip those last 3 lines, things can get messed up:

dev.off()  says "stop writing to the PDF file"
the "cmdstr" stuff says "open filename.pdf" to your operating system.

But, if you miss the dev.off(), the PDF stays on "being written", which means it can't be opened or will be corrupted -- if you then go run more graphics or PDF commands, you will get graphics not appearing or corrupt PDFs.

The main solution is:

1. Run "dev.off()" a bunch of times until it is clear all files and graphics objects are closed.

2. Then, re-run the entirety of the pdf block (e.g. like the above code) at once.

Cheers!
Nick
